Abstract: Here, the authors combine first-principles dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT), epitaxial materials design, angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, and scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy to show that superconductivity in monolayer FeSe/SrTiO 3 is maximized at a magic FeSe 4 tetrahedral angle. They demonstrate that strong electronic correlations, captured by DMFT, substantially enhance electron-phonon coupling within the FeSe layer and produce a superconducting dome. These findings reveal the microscopic origin of enhanced superconductivity and suggest a route for engineering higher-temperature superconductors.
